prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1075; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a side impact at a signalized intersection. The claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: The driver is named on the policy. Police records and statements from people at the scene confirm the claimant was riding in the vehicle at the time of the collision.

Entry 3: Initial photos of the vehicle show damage concentrated on the side that was struck, which is mostly in line with the impact described.

Entry 4: Scene photos confirm some details of the layout and final rest positions, but no independent witnesses have come forward beyond the people who were present.

Entry 5: The claimant reports neck and back strain from the collision. Medical records have been requested, and it is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.

Entry 6: A neighbor told the field contact that the car looked damaged a short time before the claimed date of loss. A follow-up interview has been scheduled to look into this statement.

Entry 7: No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from the prior claims and inspection records checked so far.

Entry 8: The claimant's account was restated through counsel. Some small details were added, but the core account of the collision has stayed the same.

Entry 9: Treatment records show a usual course of physical therapy and chiropractic visits, with appointments tapering off as the claimant improved.

Entry 10: No earlier injury to the neck or back has been identified in the claimant's history so far. The records search is still continuing.

Entry 11: Damage review is complete. The overall extent of the damage is consistent with the impact as described by the parties.

Entry 12: The file stays open pending the outstanding medical records and the neighbor follow-up. Reserve review is set for the next cycle.
